tier1Summary:
Iran and the US are trading threats over the blockade. [[p:Donald Trump]] says any ship that runs it will be sunk, and Tehran vows 'all available means' to stop it while Qatar carries messages between them. Seven tankers have been hit in a week. In Yemen, the [[p:Houthis]] are massing to encircle Aden, and an airstrike in Lahj killed 26.

In Israel, [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] {{note: Former IDF chief of staff (2015–2019) who entered politics with Benny Gantz's National Unity in 2022.}} is negotiating with [[p:Likud]] but threatens a minority government. Gaza's ceasefire is eroding under Israel's central push, and the UN has no plan after [[p:United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon|UNIFIL]].

Elsewhere, NATO sends an AWACS to Poland, Russia is reportedly ready to put a nuclear weapon in orbit, and drones hit a UN compound in Khartoum.

segmentItems.text: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman [[p:Esmaeil Baghaei|Esmail Baghaei]] vowed 'all available means' against the US blockade after [[p:Donald Trump]] threatened to sink any Iranian ship that runs it. Tehran says Hormuz reopens only if sanctions and the [[e:2026 United States naval blockade of Iran|blockade]] end and the [[e:Islamabad Talks|Islamabad]] memorandum is honoured.

Qatari envoys spent two hours in Tehran on 20 Nov, and Qatar's PM was due to meet [[p:Marco Rubio]] on 23 Nov. [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] says talking about Hormuz is pointless until Iran's demands are met.
Seven tankers have been hit since 16 Nov, three of them off Khasab in Oman, and a Jordanian sailor is missing. Brent is above $92.

An airstrike in Lahj killed 26, 12 of them [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] fighters and 14 civilians in a passing bus and truck, local officials told AFP. The Houthis blame Saudi Arabia; the government blames the Houthis.
The Houthis are massing on the Al-Bayda–Abyan front and aircraft have been striking them. A government-aligned politician says the aim is to encircle Aden rather than storm it.

[[p:Gadi Eisenkot]]'s party and [[p:Likud]] held coalition talks without a deal. Likud wants no Arab parties and Israel to keep 'security zones' in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza; Eisenkot threatens a minority emergency government instead.
Settlers torched homes and cars near Ramallah. Eisenkot called it 'Jewish terrorism' and blamed [[p:Itamar Ben-Gvir]] and [[p:Bezalel Smotrich]].

After Israel's 18 Nov push into central Gaza, drone strikes killed at least seven on 20 Nov. On 21 Nov a strike on a vehicle carrying food killed three; the IDF says they were [[p:Palestinian Islamic Jihad]] members.
segmentItems.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan

segmentItems.text: The [[p:United Nations Security Council|Security Council]] backed [[p:United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon|UNIFIL]] {{note: UN peacekeeping force created in 1978 by Security Council Resolutions 425 and 426 after Israel's invasion of southern Lebanon.}} but named no successor. The US wants an amended [[e:United Nations Security Council Resolution 1701|Resolution 1701]], and France is drafting a new text.
segmentItems.thread: Lebanon: Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli occupation

segmentItems.text: In a reportedly Iran-brokered deal, a joint force of army, police and [[p:Popular Mobilization Forces|PMF]] brigades is replacing [[p:Kata'ib Hezbollah]] at Jurf al-Sakhar. Analysts are split on whether it changes anything.

Courts upheld the cancellation of [[p:Ekrem İmamoğlu]]'s degree, which presidential candidates need, and jailed him again over the 2023 CHP vote. The [[p:Constitutional Court of Turkey|Constitutional Court]] reviews his detention on 26 Nov.
segmentItems.thread: Turkey fund crisis and opposition crackdown

tier1Check.text: After the [[p:North Atlantic Council]] met over the Russian missiles that hit Poland, Warsaw says NATO is sending an AWACS aircraft. Requests for F-35s and air defence are still under review.

NATO intelligence services believe Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite this year, German media report. That would breach the [[e:Outer Space Treaty]] {{note: 1967 treaty, drafted at the UN and signed by the US, UK and Soviet Union, that bans nuclear weapons in orbit.}}.
Drones hit homes and a UN compound in Khartoum. The UN points to the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]]; Sudan's army claims the drones flew from Ethiopia.

readInFull.title: What next for Iraq's push against militias following Jurf al-Sakhar deal?
readInFull.why: Explains how Baghdad got [[p:Kata'ib Hezbollah]] to let the state into its stronghold, the reported Iranian role, and why analysts disagree on whether the deal changes anything.

readInFull.title: Yemen's war fronts expand as Houthis attempt to encircle Aden
readInFull.why: Aden-based reporting on the new Al-Bayda–Abyan front, showing how the [[p:Houthis]] could squeeze Aden from two directions rather than storm it.

watchThisWeek.text: Duma third reading of Russia's 2027–29 budget, 24 Nov.
Kazakhstan: government anti-corruption proposals for state companies due to [[p:Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]].
Belgium: [[p:Bart De Wever]] reports to the King on the federal budget, 23 Nov, the day of a national union demonstration.
Outcome of the extraordinary [[p:North Atlantic Council]] meeting on the Russian missiles that hit Poland: more air defence and jets for the eastern flank?
Malaysia: whether Anwar accepts Anthony Loke's resignation, and BN's push for an early general election after Melaka.
Pakistan: Islamabad High Court hearing of [[p:Imran Khan]] and Bushra Bibi's appeals in the £190m Al-Qadir Trust case.
Sweden: Speaker's round with party leaders and Kristersson's final report, 24 Nov; a third PM vote may follow.
Moldova's energy state of emergency expires on 24 Nov: extension or not.
Extraordinary European Council on the 2028–34 MFF negotiating box, 26 Nov, ahead of a target deal at the 17–18 Dec summit.
Pakistan: Islamabad High Court hearing on constituency boundaries that decides whether Islamabad's local elections (rescheduled for 20 Dec) go ahead.
Armenia: publication of the draft new constitution, Azerbaijan's condition for signing the peace treaty.
Venezuela: 24-hour public-sector strike and march on Miraflores over wages and the year-end bonus.
South Africa: new councils elect mayors in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, where an ANC–ActionSA–MK–EFF bloc may shut out the DA.
France: joint committee on the 2027 social security budget, 26 Nov, when the 50-day deadline expires; 49.3 or ordinance possible.
Turkey: [[p:Constitutional Court of Turkey|Constitutional Court]] plenary takes up [[p:Ekrem İmamoğlu]]'s application against his pretrial detention, 26 Nov.
Georgia: opposition's nationwide rally in Tbilisi.
Serbia: Speaker Aleksandar Čupić calls the presidential election (20 or 27 Dec) by 27 Nov.
Taiwan local elections, 28 Nov, amid PLA pressure and Lai's warnings of Chinese interference.
Algeria local (APC/APW) elections, 28 Nov.
Kazakhstan: snap maslikhat (local council) elections for 3,447 seats.
Iran's convoy of 14+ tankers off Kharg Island tries to run the US naval blockade.
Canada–US trade agreement after the restart of talks.
Spain general election, 29 Nov.
Rodrigo Duterte's ICC crimes-against-humanity trial opens in The Hague, 30 Nov.
Ecuador local elections (prefects, mayors, councillors, CPCCS), with Noboa campaigning for ADN.
Europe names its delegation (three to five officials) for the next round of Ukraine peace talks.
Gagauzia bashkan runoff on 29 Nov: [[p:Alexandr Stoianoglo]] against the Socialists' Fiodor Gagauz.
Apex committee meeting of the Pakistan–Saudi–Turkey [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]] in Islamabad.
Maldives: final votes on the Ras Malé real-estate bill and three other government bills, and the opposition MDP's referendum rally.
Commission formally tables the 22nd Russia sanctions package; Denmark proposes an EU-wide tourist visa ban on Russians.
Possible visit by the French, German and British national security advisers to Moscow at [[p:Yuri Ushakov]]'s invitation.
Bangladesh: [[p:Sheikh Hasina]]'s stated plan to return from India in December, India's extradition decision and further Awami League lockdowns.
Israel: whether [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] brings a minority 'national emergency government' to a Knesset vote if Likud talks fail.
